subject: Proposal: accelerated annualization and SLA offset for mid-contract expansion
messages:
From: Sara Whitman <sara@pulseentry.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco@pulseentry.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mid-contract capacity increase + co-term question

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering workload spiked faster than expected and we need to expand capacity immediately. We have two asks we want to surface up front:

1) Can Redwood support a mid-contract uplift for Q4 usage (estimated +40% run-rate) and co-term it to our existing Mar 31 renewal?
2) Given the timing, Procurement is asking for a modest discount or credit to offset the partial-term billing (they view mid-cycle additions as a premium). We understand supply is constrained but wanted to see what flexibility exists — either an effective discount or a performance credit tied to latency SLOs.

We can share a short mutual action plan and a PO number once terms are agreed. Attached a one-page note on our expected usage profile and priority SLA windows.

Can you share a couple of structure options (accelerated annualization vs. staged top-up credits) plus the legal/PO timeline? We need an answer before our Nov 30 board meeting.

— Sara Whitman
CTO, PulseEntry Inc.
(sara@pulseentry.com)

Attachment: PulseEntry_usage_profile_Q4_v2.xlsx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Whitman <sara@pulseentry.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marco Diaz <marco@pulseentry.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity increase + co-term question

Sara —

Thanks for the clear note and the usage attachment. Quick response with two pragmatic options we typically use for mid-contract expansion. I copied Aditya (commercial), Lauren (billing), and Priyom (legal) to accelerate.

Option A — Accelerated annualization (preferred if PulseEntry wants a clean co-term):
- PulseEntry commits to the uplift as an annualized run-rate for the remainder of the fiscal year; we convert the uplifted units into an accelerated term and co-term everything to Mar 31.
- Commercial concession: one-time effective discount of 8% on the uplifted portion (applied as a credit on the next invoice).
- SLA offset: we offer a performance credit (token-based) if latency SLOs > target during the first 60 days after uplift.

Option B — Staged top-up credits (lower commitment, more flexible):
- Add uplift as a mid-contract top-up billed prorata. PulseEntry receives monthly consumption credits up to 10% of uplifted billed tokens for the first 3 months if usage and SLOs meet agreed thresholds.
- No change to renewal date (co-term still possible via a small amendment) but fewer upfront concessions.

Operational notes: legal drat an amendment and a short SLA addendum — attached a starter draft (redwood-amendment-draft.docx) and a one-sheet pricing model (PulseEntry_SLA-offset-proposal.xlsx). If you prefer Option A we can target a DocuSign routing within 48 hours after PO.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm preference A or B by EOD Tue Nov 24 (board timeline).
- If A, Aditya will send the final commercial sheet and I’ll loop Priyom for the amendment redlines.
- If B, we can finalize a 3-month ramp and waive the co-term penalty; billing to follow.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood-amendment-draft.docx, PulseEntry_SLA-offset-proposal.xlsx

From: Marco Diaz <marco@pulseentry.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sara Whitman <sara@pulseentry.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity increase + co-term question

Hannah / team —

Thanks for the quick options. Procurement has two clarifying asks before we can present either to Finance:

1) If we go with Option A (accelerated annualization) we need the effective discount to be shown as a line on the amendment and not as an opaque credit. Finance requires a clear net effective discount to approve PO issuance.
2) If there is an SLA performance credit, define the measurement (90th percentile p95 latency window, monitoring hook, and credit calculation). We need measurable metrics tied to billing.

We also prefer invoice timing spelled out: can Redwood invoice the uplift immediately and apply the credit on the following invoice, or do you invoice pro rata and show the adjustment in the same invoice cycle? Either approach works, but we need clarity for cashflow modeling.

I’m attaching Procurement_Req.pdf with our PO steps and approval thresholds.

— Marco Diaz
Sourcing Manager, PulseEntry Inc.
Attachment: Procurement_Req.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: guidance on PulseEntry asks

Team —

Recapping client asks and my recommended commercial stance so we can move quickly:

Client asks: mid-contract +40% uplift, co-term to Mar 31, wants a visible discount or credit, and measurable SLA credits. Procurement wants invoice clarity for PO.

Recommended (commercial):
- Approve Option A as structured by Hannah but increase the effective discount to 10% on uplifted ARR rather than 8% (comply with their board ask and accelerate close).
- SLA credit: define as 5% of that month’s uplifted invoice for any month where p95 latency > 600ms across the production window, measured by our tracing hooks. (Priyom — please translate into legal-friendly SLA language in the amendment.)
- Invoice flow: invoice uplift pro rata immediately; show the 10% discount as a line-item credit on the following invoice so finance has a clear audit trail. Lauren — confirm this is operationally OK.

Risk tolerance: Do not go beyond 12% discount without exec approval; keep credit cap to 2 months of uplift billing to limit exposure.

If we agree, Hannah should send a short commercial sheet to Marco+Sara with the numbers and then Priyom to issue a 1–2 page amendment. Target: have signed amendment and PO by Nov 30.

Thanks — Aditya
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Sara / Marco —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on internal alignment here’s what we can commit to for an expedited close:

- We will move forward with Option A (accelerated annualization) and apply a 10% effective discount on the uplifted portion, shown as a line-item credit in the subsequent invoice (so your Finance team has a clean PO/invoice pairing).
- SLA measurement: Redwood will instrument p95 latency measured by our tracing endpoint (production window defined 06:00–22:00 PT). If p95 > 600ms for a calendar month, PulseEntry receives a 5% credit on that month’s uplifted invoice, up to a maximum of two months of uplift billing. Priyom will add the exact measurement query in the amendment.
- Timing & legal: Priyom will circulate a 1–2 page amendment redline within 24 hours; Aditya will send the commercial summary with adjusted numbers. Once you sign the amendment and provide a PO we’ll spin up the additional pool.

Would you prefer a short call tomorrow to confirm the PO path and timing? We are standing by to route DocuSign as soon as Procurement confirms invoice preference.

Best regards,
